law_name: Zustrombegrenzungsgesetz (draft 'Influx Limitation Act') and five-point migration motion
description: As opposition leader, Merz had the CDU/CSU group table a five-point migration motion and push to a vote its bill to limit migration (reinstating limitation of immigration as a goal of the Residence Act, suspending family reunification for people with subsidiary protection and extending Federal Police powers) after the Aschaffenburg attack. The motion was adopted on 29 January 2025 with AfD and FDP votes; the bill was rejected on 31 January 2025 by 338 votes to 349.
significance: The first Bundestag majority secured with AfD votes, which triggered nationwide protests and criticism from Angela Merkel; several elements resurfaced in the 2025 coalition agreement.

law_name: Amendment of the Basic Law: debt-brake reform and €500 billion special fund (new Article 143h)
description: Negotiated by Merz with the SPD and the Greens after the February 2025 election and adopted by the outgoing Bundestag on 18 March 2025 (512 votes) and the Bundesrat on 21 March 2025. Defence and certain security spending above 1% of GDP is exempt from the debt brake, the Länder may borrow 0.35% of GDP, and a debt-financed special fund of €500 billion for infrastructure and climate neutrality was created, with €100 billion for the Länder and €100 billion for the Climate and Transformation Fund.
significance: The fiscal basis of the Merz government's rearmament and investment programme; it reversed the CDU/CSU campaign pledge to keep the debt brake unchanged.

law_name: Act suspending family reunification for persons entitled to subsidiary protection
description: Coalition bill adopted by the Bundestag on 27 June 2025 (444 to 133), suspending family reunification for people with subsidiary protection for two years, with hardship exceptions, and writing the goal of limiting immigration into the Residence Act.
significance: One of the first migration laws of the Merz government, implementing a CDU/CSU campaign pledge.

law_name: Gesetz für ein steuerliches Investitionssofortprogramm zur Stärkung des Wirtschaftsstandorts Deutschland ('investment booster')
description: Passed by the Bundestag in June 2025 and approved by the Bundesrat on 11 July 2025: up to 30% declining-balance depreciation for equipment acquired from July 2025 to December 2027, faster write-offs for electric company cars, and a cut in corporation tax from 15% to 10% in five annual steps from 2028.
significance: The government's main supply-side tax measure, with an estimated revenue loss of almost €46 billion over 2025–2029.

law_name: Amendment of the Nationality Act (abolition of 'turbo naturalisation')
description: Adopted by the Bundestag on 8 October 2025: abolishes the possibility, introduced in 2024, of naturalisation after three years for particularly well-integrated applicants, so that naturalisation again requires at least five years of residence; dual citizenship remains possible.
significance: Implements a coalition-agreement commitment while keeping the rest of the 2024 citizenship reform.

description: Adopted by the Bundestag on 5 December 2025 (323 to 272) and in force since 1 January 2026: introduces registration and medical screening for men born from 2008 while keeping military service voluntary, with Bundeswehr growth targets to 2035 and the option of a needs-based compulsory service by further law.
significance: Germany's first major change to military service since conscription was suspended in 2011, part of Merz's goal of making the Bundeswehr Europe's strongest conventional army.

law_name: Pension package 2025 (Rentenpaket: 48% pension level, Mütterrente, Aktivrente)
description: Adopted by the Bundestag on 5 December 2025 with 318 votes: fixes the pension level at 48% until 2031, fully equalises child-rearing credits for children born before 1992 ('Mütterrente') and, through the Aktivrente law, makes up to €2,000 a month of wages tax-free for employees working past the statutory retirement age from 1 January 2026.
significance: Delivered core coalition pension pledges after a dispute with the Junge Union; Merz insisted on reaching the chancellor majority.

law_name: Steueränderungsgesetz 2025 (7% VAT on restaurant food, commuter allowance, farm diesel)
description: Approved by the Bundesrat on 19 December 2025, effective 1 January 2026: VAT on restaurant food reduced permanently from 19% to 7% (drinks excluded), commuter allowance of 38 cents from the first kilometre, reinstatement of the agricultural diesel tax refund and higher allowances for volunteers.
significance: Implemented several specific coalition tax pledges on the promised date.

law_name: 13th Act amending Book II of the Social Code (Neue Grundsicherung / Grundsicherungsgeld)
description: Adopted by the Bundestag on 5 March 2026 and in force since 1 July 2026: replaces the Bürgergeld with the 'Grundsicherungsgeld', with priority for job placement, stricter obligations, three-month benefit cuts for breaches and tighter rules on protected assets and housing costs.
significance: Fulfilled a central CDU campaign pledge; welfare associations criticised it as a step backwards, while employers welcomed it.

law_name: Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz (reform of the Building Energy Act / 'heating law')
description: Cabinet draft of 13 May 2026, adopted by the Bundestag on 10 July 2026 (323 to 271): removes the requirement that new heating systems use 65% renewable energy, allows oil and gas heating to continue to be installed and operated in the long term, and renames the Gebäudeenergiegesetz as Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz, in force since 29 July 2026.
significance: Reversed the previous government's most controversial climate law, as promised by the CDU; an assessment by the Bundestag's research services reported by tagesschau raised constitutional doubts in view of Germany's climate obligations.

law_name: July 2026 reform package: pension reform and Einkommensteuerreformgesetz 2027 (pending)
description: On 1–2 July 2026 the coalition committee chaired by Merz endorsed implementing all 33 recommendations of the pension commission (retirement age linked to life expectancy after 2031, abolition of deduction-free retirement after 45 contribution years, a mandatory funded pension component) and an income tax reform worth about €10 billion a year in relief, partly financed by higher top rates. The income tax bill was adopted by the cabinet on 2 September 2026; as of October 2026 neither part has been enacted.
significance: Presented by Merz as his central reform agenda, to be legislated by the end of 2026; resistance from the SPD after the September 2026 state elections made it a focus of the coalition crisis.
